`apply-zh.html` is the application for a public posting, `https://app.eightfold.ai/careers/apply?pid=68763148348&domain=eightfold.ai`, as Eightfold's own page code drew it on 2026-10-20 for a browser that asks for Chinese (`zh-CN`), before anything was typed: a look-only visit was recorded, and the recording was played back on this machine with every request to Eightfold answered from it. Nothing was filled, uploaded, agreed to or sent on Eightfold's site. Only the page's title and its `<form>` are kept; scripts, styles, images and icons are taken out.

Eightfold draws in the visitor's language, which it takes from the browser's (`hl=zh-CN` on its own requests): the form's own fields (email, names, phone, country, city, resume) come labeled in Chinese from its server, the employer's questions keep their English question but show their choices in Chinese, and the country list names countries in Chinese. What stays as it was written is each field's id (`_____email`, `_____phone-country-code`…) and each choice's `data-test-id` (`<question id>-<choice>`) and `aria-label` (`<choice>, <question>`), which is what the adapter goes by.

Seen in the played-back page, and not kept in this one: the phone number takes only digits, dashes and brackets (its country code is chosen apart); a field left in the same moment it is typed into says "can't be blank" until it is left again; uploading a resume first asks the visitor to agree to the data privacy policy, which is theirs to do; a sent application shows `#form-submission-success-message` in a dialog over the form. The State field that a country can bring up wasn't drawn: its list comes from a request the recording doesn't hold.
